Here, the authors demonstrate controllable and tunable coupling in PbTe–Pb hybrid nanowires. More importantly, they establish a direct connection between the coupling strength and the emergence of robust zero modes. These findings provide valuable insights into engineering Majorana zero modes in this promising material platform.

summary: A quantum point contact between fractional quantum Hall states with different fillings can act as a dissipationless voltage transformer and provide a physical realization of the boundary sine-Gordon model. Here, the authors use analytical and tensor network calculations of a sliding charge density wave to solve this open problem and quantitatively connect the conductance to the boundary sine-Gordon model.
